PROOF-1.after: claude plugin marketplace add https://github.com/rlabarca/purlin --scope project
PROOF-1.before: claude plugin marketplace add https://github.com/rlabarca/purlin.git --scope project
PROOF-1.case: the install lines under "Install" in README.md and under step 1 of docs/getting-started.md; the proof says they are the same lines and the address reads https://github.com/rlabarca/purlin.git; the changed README gives https://github.com/rlabarca/purlin, so the lines differ and the address is not the

explanation: PROOF-1: the test reads the install lines of both pages, asserts the two lists are equal and asserts that the marketplace address of each is exactly the one in ADDRESS, which is what the proof names.

PROOF-1: the expected address is the constant ADDRESS, whose value is not in the test's own lines, so the test checks the proof's address only if that constant holds `https://github.com/rlabarca/purlin.git`.
PROOF-1: the three helpers that pick out the lines and the address are not shown, so a helper that trims or normalises what it reads could make two different lines compare equal.

PROOF-1: the test also asserts that a block under another heading gives no install lines and that a one-word difference makes the lists unequal, which guards the helper and the comparison and is outside the proof's own case.
PROOF-1: the proof does nothing before it observes, since it reads two pages as they stand, which fits a rule about what the pages say.
Findings: none, and the test shows no pattern a spot test would flag: it asserts, each assertion can fail, and its expected address comes from a constant and not from the pages.

PROOF-2.case: an empty project where the getting-started page's install commands run against this checkout; the proof says `claude plugin list` shows `purlin@purlin` installed and enabled for that project; the changed page's install command names a marketplace that does not exist, so nothing is installed

explanation: PROOF-2: the test asks for the install inside its own body, then reads the plugin's row as enabled, at project scope and at the test project's path, which is what the proof names as installed and enabled for that project.
PROOF-2: the test also runs `claude plugin list` and looks for `purlin@purlin` and `enabled` anywhere in the output, so those two words need not stand on the same line or belong to the same project.

PROOF-2: the source of the fixture that runs the commands is not shown, so the test's own lines do not say which page's commands are run or whether both pages are read; a wrong command on a page the fixture does not read would still pass.
PROOF-2: the spot tests found nothing, and the test holds failable assertions on the values the proof names.

PROOF-3.case: the install of PROOF-2 from this checkout; the proof says the folder the installed plugin reads its skills from holds a `SKILL.md` for each folder under `skills/`; the changed manifest names `skills/audit` as that folder, which holds a `SKILL.md` for none of them

explanation: PROOF-3: the test reads the installed plugin's manifest to find the one folder it reads skills from, and requires that folder to be a real folder inside the installed plugin.

PROOF-3: it requires the folders there that hold a `SKILL.md` to be exactly the checkout's skill folders, then compares each installed `SKILL.md` with the checkout's as bytes, which is what the proof names.

PROOF-3: both sides of the byte comparison come from the same checkout, so a change to a skill's text travels to both and cannot break the proof; only a change to where the skills land or are read from can.
PROOF-3: the count check of at least 9 skills and the "no other skill" comparison go beyond what the proof names and keep an empty or partial listing from passing.
PROOF-3: the spot tests found nothing, and the test as written leaves no way past it for a change to the covered files.

PROOF-4.after:
description: Report what a pull, a merge, a rebase or a checkout changed in the rules, the proofs and the tests, and name a number two branches both took
disable-model-invocation: true
PROOF-4.before: description: Report what a pull, a merge, a rebase or a checkout changed in the rules, the proofs and the tests, and name a number two branches both took
PROOF-4.case: after the install, the one prompt asks the smallest model to list the slash commands that start purlin:; the proof says the answer names every skill folder under skills/; with the change the drift skill is not offered to the model, so the answer leaves out drift

explanation: PROOF-4: the test runs the one prompt in the installed project, requires a zero exit and an answer that is not an error, reads each `purlin:` name whole from the answer and asserts that no folder under `skills/` is missing from those names, which is what the proof names.
PROOF-4: the expected names come from the folders on disk and not from the answer, so a skill the model is no longer offered fails the test unless the model names it anyway.
PROOF-4: the test asserts at least 9 skill folders where the files shown hold 10, so that count would not notice one folder being removed, though the proof speaks only of the folders that are there.
PROOF-4: the test shown does not itself check that the smallest model is the one asked; that lies in the helper that builds the prompt.

PROOF-5.case: the install as the README gives it, in a fresh project; the proof says the person's own list of installed plugins reads the same before and after; the changed install puts purlin in the person's own list, so it differs

explanation: PROOF-5: the test reads the person's own plugins and marketplaces after the install and compares each with the reading taken before, which is the comparison the proof names.
PROOF-5: the test compares only those two lists, so a change the install made to the person's other settings, which the rule also names, would still pass.
PROOF-5: the test deletes the base folder itself and then asserts the project folder is gone, so that assertion observes the test's own clean-up and not anything the install did.
PROOF-5: the before reading and the install come from a fixture not shown, so whether the install follows the README, the getting-started page or both cannot be read from the test's own lines.
PROOF-5: the spot tests found nothing, and nothing in the test's own lines contradicts that: both comparisons can fail and the expected values come from a reading taken before the install.
notes: PROOF-5 names "the test's project folder is deleted afterwards", which describes the test's own mechanics and not something a person installing would see.
